description:
The US Vice President says authorities are investigating a deadly strike on a wedding in southern Iran, but that he is 'sceptical' about claims America was involved.
 
It comes as the head of Iran's Revolutionary Guard has vowed to 'avenge' those killed in the blast at the celebrations in Kuhestak.
 
Elsewhere there are questions about Pete Hegseth's leadership of the Pentagon as a series of military leaders are removed or forced out.
 
And the price of oil rises once again, as the US and Iran return to trading strikes.

description:
Today, we discuss the economic challenges Andy Burnham is facing ahead of his first budget.   

The economic backdrop has left the prime minister and his Chancellor John Healey with big decisions to make about defence spending, as pressure increases on the government to raise it. Adam Fleming is joined by economics editor Faisal Islam and Helen Miller, director at the IFS to discuss the options for the government.   

Plus, the BBC’s technology and AI editor Zoe Kleinman is the first British journalist to hail a self-driving Uber in London. She’s in the studio to debrief on what the journey was like, and how quickly the technology is evolving.

Elon Musk’s X alleges that China has been stirring up a backlash against American data centres. 

Israel and Russia have denied allegations from Spain’s prime minister that they’re partly to blame for the migrant crisis in Ceuta. 

And Germany has accused Russia of being behind a spate of drone attacks at a German airport. Vladimir Putin has dismissed those claims and accused Germany of a‘ false flag’ operation.

author: BBC News
description:
Londoners are able to hail the UK's first robotaxis - as Uber today becomes the first company to launch a self-driving minicab.
 
Initially, it only has 15 autonomous vehicles with a licence to operate in the city, and each one must have a human safety driver behind the wheel ready to take control if anything goes wrong.
 
Uber said it surveyed London-based customers via the app and more than 100,000 said they would choose a self-driving taxi if one was available, despite incidents of driverless rides malfunctioning in US cities where they already operate.

author: BBC News
description:
A BBC investigation has found criminal groups who illegally smuggle people to the UK across the English Channel are running low on small boats. 
 
Gang members have told BBC sources that rival factions are now having to work together to load migrants on fewer, larger vessels. They’re also charging them more. 
 
The number of crossings is currently at a six-year-low and UK ministers have credited the French police for intercepting more attempts. 
 
The BBC’s Paris Correspondent James Waterhouse has looked at how the people smugglers are being forced to adapt.

Gloria Steinem, who became a face of the women's liberation movement in the US, has died, aged 92.
 
In a post on Instagram, her foundation said she "passed away peacefully" at her home in New York City on Wednesday, "surrounded by many who loved her".
 
Steinem, who was a writer and magazine editor, co-founded the Women's Action Alliance - a group dedicated to fighting sexism - more than 50 years ago.
